title: Cap Automator cooldowns throttle only increases, leaving risk reduction instantaneous
content:
The cooldown is defined asymmetrically. A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3 permits a cap update "as long as the resulting exposure does not exceed the specified maximum limit **and the cooldown period has elapsed in the case of increases**." A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.1.2 confirms it: `ttl` is "the minimum time requirement before it is possible to increase the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap."

Nothing gates a decrease. Caps can be cut to the current usage level at any moment, repeatedly, with no waiting.

This is the correct shape for any safety limit, and it is easy to get wrong. A symmetric cooldown would mean that after an emergency reduction, capacity could not be restored quickly — but far worse, it would mean an attacker who inflated a cap just before the cooldown started could hold that inflated ceiling for the full window while defenders wait out their own brake.

With the asymmetry, the worst case is bounded by arithmetic: exposure can only expand by `gap` per `ttl` interval. The live configurations put that between 4 and 12 hours (A.6.1.1.1.3.2.1.1.3.2.1 through .3.2.15), so even an attacker controlling the authorized party must spend days to build a large position — days during which any observer can cut the cap back instantly.

It is the same principle as the Spark Liquidity Layer's `slope`: constrain the rate at which risk can grow, never the rate at which it can shrink.
description: The ttl gate applies 'in the case of increases to the Supply Cap or Borrow Cap'; lowering a cap needs no elapsed time, so the brake is always faster than the accelerator.
